args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After v2.3.1 was deployed, checkout-api started failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to redeploy it, and check why a release that failed in staging still went to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is passing health checks again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0002, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** After the v2.3.1 deploy, the service was unhealthy in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The first attempt to create it timed out. I checked the incident list, found nothing had been created, then retried, so there's only one incident and one page. It describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-ups below.

Two things to follow up:
- **Why v2.3.1 failed:** Find the cause before anyone tries to deploy it again.
- **How it reached production:** The v2.3.1 release candidate had also failed health checks in staging, so it's worth checking why it went to production anyway.
